faqs.question: How much does custom software development cost?
faqs.answer: The cost depends on features, technical complexity, integrations, and delivery requirements. I can discuss your requirements before defining a scope and estimate.

faqs.question: Do I need a complete specification?
faqs.answer: No. A clear description of the problem, intended users, and desired functionality is a useful starting point.

faqs.question: When does custom software make sense?
faqs.answer: When teams rely on spreadsheets, disconnected systems, or repetitive manual tasks, purpose-built software can help bring the work into a more structured process.

title: ERP & Operations Software
description: Systems that centralize orders, inventory, approvals, reporting, and operational workflows.
heroTitle: ERP and operations software that centralizes real work.
heroLead: Many businesses run on spreadsheets, chat threads, and disconnected tools. I develop custom ERP-style and operations systems that bring orders, inventory, approvals, permissions, audit trails, and reporting into one practical application shaped around your processes.

usefulWhen.title: Work is scattered across spreadsheets and chat
usefulWhen.description: Orders, stock, approvals, and status updates live in different places, so nobody trusts a single source of truth.

usefulWhen.title: Reporting takes too long
usefulWhen.description: Managers spend hours assembling status from exports instead of reviewing a shared operational view.

usefulWhen.title: Permissions and accountability are unclear
usefulWhen.description: Too many people can change records, or important changes leave no usable history.

deliverables.title: Operational workflows
deliverables.description: Structured paths for requests, handoffs, status updates, and approvals across teams.

deliverables.title: Inventory and order visibility
deliverables.description: Shared records for stock, orders, or operational items so teams stop reconciling conflicting spreadsheets.

deliverables.title: Role-based access
deliverables.description: Permissions that control what each role can view and change.

deliverables.title: Reporting and dashboards
deliverables.description: Views that help managers see status, bottlenecks, and exceptions without manual report assembly.

deliverables.title: Audit trails
deliverables.description: Records of important changes so activity can be reviewed later.

deliverables.title: Integrations when needed
deliverables.description: Connections to existing ERPs, accounting tools, or external APIs when the system must exchange data.

process.title: Map the operational work
process.description: Identify users, decisions, current tools, and the bottlenecks that waste the most time.

process.title: Define the first release
process.description: Choose the workflows, roles, and reports that must work in the initial system.

process.title: Build and review
process.description: Develop modules with visible progress and feedback checkpoints.

process.title: Test with real scenarios
process.description: Validate permissions, handoffs, and reporting against actual operating cases.

process.title: Launch and expand
process.description: Release the first useful system, then plan additional modules as requirements become clearer.

relatedProjects.label: Business operations and reporting
relatedProjects.name: DOME
relatedProjects.description: Operations workflows, access permissions, audit trails, and reporting in one system.

relatedProjects.label: Warehouse production
relatedProjects.name: WPS

faqs.question: Do I need a full ERP, or a focused operations system?
faqs.answer: Not every business needs a large packaged ERP. Many companies get better results from a focused system that covers the workflows causing the most friction first, then expands later.

faqs.question: Can you work with an existing ERP such as SAP Business One?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some projects improve or extend an existing ERP with custom portals, dashboards, or integrations. Others replace spreadsheet-based processes with a purpose-built operations application.

faqs.question: How does a project start?
faqs.answer: Share the operational problem, the users involved, and any current tools. I review suitability, discuss scope if it looks like a fit, and agree next steps before a proposal.

title: Warehouse Management Software
description: Receiving, GRN processing, inventory visibility, and dock-to-stock warehouse workflows.
heroTitle: Warehouse software that reduces manual receiving and inventory work.
heroLead: Many warehouses still rely on paper GRNs, spreadsheets, and re-keying into an ERP. I build custom warehouse management software for receiving, purchase-order checks, inventory visibility, labeling, and floor workflows—so dock and stock data stay consistent.

usefulWhen.title: Dock work is still paper-heavy
usefulWhen.description: GRNs and packing slips are typed into spreadsheets or ERP screens after the fact, which slows receiving and introduces errors.

usefulWhen.title: Inventory counts disagree
usefulWhen.description: Floor, purchasing, and finance each maintain different views of what arrived and what is available.

usefulWhen.title: Exceptions are hard to catch
usefulWhen.description: Short shipments, wrong SKUs, and PO mismatches are discovered late because there is no shared receiving workflow.

deliverables.title: Receiving and GRN workflows
deliverables.description: Structured paths for goods receipt notes, packing slips, and inbound checks instead of paper-only dock processes.

deliverables.title: Purchase-order matching
deliverables.description: Compare inbound quantities and lines against open POs so mismatches are visible before stock is committed.

deliverables.title: Inventory visibility
deliverables.description: Shared records for received stock, locations, and status so teams stop reconciling conflicting spreadsheets.

deliverables.title: Batch and lot tracking
deliverables.description: Capture batch, lot, or expiry details when the operation requires them.

deliverables.title: Labels and scanning support
deliverables.description: Barcode or label steps that fit dock and floor devices when hardware is part of the process.

deliverables.title: ERP and system connections
deliverables.description: Push verified receipts and inventory updates into SAP Business One or other systems when integration is required.

process.title: Map dock and floor work
process.description: Review receiving steps, documents, exceptions, devices, and where data is entered today.

process.title: Define the first release
process.description: Choose the receiving, matching, and visibility features that must work before broader WMS modules.

process.title: Build and review
process.description: Develop the console and integrations with checkpoints against real shipment scenarios.

process.title: Test with operational cases
process.description: Validate mismatches, partial receipts, labeling, and ERP commits with sample dock work.

process.title: Launch and expand
process.description: Release the first useful warehouse workflows, then plan put-away, transfers, or reporting next.

relatedProjects.label: Warehouse production
relatedProjects.name: WPS
relatedProjects.description: Warehouse production workflows with scanning, reporting, and SAP Business One integration.

relatedProjects.label: Enterprise ERP
relatedProjects.name: DOME
relatedProjects.description: Centralized operations platform covering inventory, supply chain, and reporting modules.

faqs.question: Do I need a full commercial WMS?
faqs.answer: Not always. Many operations get more value from focused warehouse software that covers receiving, GRN processing, and inventory visibility first, then expands only where the floor still has friction.

faqs.question: Can this connect to SAP Business One or another ERP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some projects commit verified receipts into an existing ERP. Others keep a warehouse console as the working layer and sync selected fields.

faqs.question: How does a project start?
faqs.answer: Share how receiving works today, which documents and systems are involved, and where re-entry or mismatches happen. I review suitability and discuss scope before a proposal.

faqs.question: Can a dashboard pull from more than one system?

faqs.question: What’s the difference between a website and a web application?
faqs.answer: A business website communicates information and helps visitors take action. A web application allows users to complete tasks, manage data, and interact with a system over time.

faqs.question: What considerations affect web project scope?
faqs.answer: Accessibility, responsive layouts, performance, account management, data handling, and integration with existing services all influence scope.

faqs.question: Can you improve an existing web application?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can review the current product, identify practical improvements, and plan changes without assuming a full rebuild.

faqs.question: Can you work on an existing application?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can review an existing system to understand its architecture, current issues, and proposed changes before determining a suitable approach.

faqs.question: Do all projects require a full rebuild?
